main.title_en: The First Tengu Was a Star | What the Oldest Sources Say
main.title_ja: 最初の天狗は、星だった
main.description_en:
The oldest Japanese record of the tengu describes a star. Follow the word from the Nihon Shoki through medieval tales of bird-like tricksters to the long-nosed masks, carvings, and prints of later centuries, and see how the bird form stayed alongside the long-nosed figure.

This video uses synthetic narration and clearly labelled AI-generated illustrations. They are atmospheric illustrations, not historical evidence or exact reconstructions of real places or sacred sites.

Chapters
00:00 The Long-Nosed Goblin
00:49 A Star That Barked
02:15 Birds That Fooled the Faithful
03:39 The Long Nose
04:58 Star, Bird, and Goblin

Sources
- W. G. Aston, Nihongi, vol. II (1896), Book XXIII, pp. 167–168 — https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi/Book_XXIII
- Nihon Shoki, vol. 23 (1926 facsimile), frame 10 — https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1182143/1/10
- Shiji, Tianguan shu (printed edition, c. 1925), frame 87 — https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/958959/1/87
- Konjaku Monogatari-shu 20-2 (transcription consulted) — https://yatanavi.org/text/k_konjaku/k_konjaku20-2
- Konjaku Monogatari-shu 20-3 (transcription consulted) — https://yatanavi.org/text/k_konjaku/k_konjaku20-3
- Uji Shui Monogatari, tale 32 (transcription consulted) — https://yatanavi.org/text/yomeiuji/uji032
References only (images not used): Tengu Zoshi (c. 1296); Zegaibo-e (c. 1354).

main.description_ja:
日本のいちばん古い記録に出てくる天狗は、星でした。『日本書紀』から、人をだます鳥の姿の中世の説話、そして長い鼻の面・根付・版画へ。鳥の姿と鼻の高い姿が並んで残ったことを、文献と資料でたどります。

この動画のナレーションは合成音声です。AIで作った再現画・再現映像には、画面にその旨を表示しています。再現は雰囲気を示す挿絵で、史料や、実在の場所・寺社の正確な復元ではありません。

チャプター
00:00 鼻の長い山の妖怪
00:49 吠える星
02:15 人をだます鳥
03:39 長い鼻
04:58 星と鳥と天狗

出典
- W. G. Aston, Nihongi, vol. II (1896), Book XXIII, pp. 167–168 — https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi/Book_XXIII

- Konjaku Monogatari-shu 20-3 (transcription consulted) — https://yatanavi.org/text/k_konjaku/k_konjaku20-3
